5815-the-great-impersonation.title: The Great Impersonation
5815-the-great-impersonation.creator: E. Phillips Oppenheim
5815-the-great-impersonation.description: A book by E. Phillips Oppenheim. I was obliged to shoot one or two, and the rest deserted. They took my compass, damn them, and I'm nearly a hundred miles out of my bearings. You couldn't give me a drink, could you?”

arxiv-2011-00527.title: A Dilated Residual Hierarchically Fashioned Segmentation Framework for Extracting Gleason Tissues and Grading Prostate Cancer from Whole Slide Images
arxiv-2011-00527.creator: Taimur Hassan, Bilal Hassan, Ayman El-Baz, Naoufel Werghi
arxiv-2011-00527.description: Abstract Prostate cancer (PCa) is the second deadliest form of cancer in males, and it can be clinically graded by examining the structural representations of Gleason tissues. This paper proposes a new method for segmenting the Gleason tissues (patch-wise) in order to grade PCa from the whole slide images (WSI).

arxiv-2101-03137.title: Evaluation of Sustainable Green Materials: Pinecone in Permeable Adsorptive Barriers for Remediation of Groundwater Contaminated by P ​ b 2 + Pb^{2+} and Methylene Blue
arxiv-2101-03137.creator: Samuel Darko, Gurcan Comert, Noelle A Mware, Faith Kibuye
arxiv-2101-03137.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Samuel Darko, Gurcan Comert, Noelle A Mware, Faith Kibuye. We report herein, the potential of raw pinecone powder (PCP) and pinecone biochar (PCBC) as alternatives to activated carbon used in Permeable Adsorptive Barriers (PABs) for the in situ remediation of polluted groundwater.

arxiv-2305-06969.title: A Survey on Intersectional Fairness in Machine Learning: Notions, Mitigation, and Challenges
arxiv-2305-06969.creator: Usman Gohar, Lu Cheng
arxiv-2305-06969.description: Abstract The widespread adoption of Machine Learning systems, especially in more decision-critical applications such as criminal sentencing and bank loans, has led to increased concerns about fairness implications. Algorithms and metrics have been developed to mitigate and measure these discriminations.

arxiv-2404-00796.title: CARL: Congestion-Aware Reinforcement Learning for Imitation-based Perturbations in Mixed Traffic Control
arxiv-2404-00796.creator: Bibek Poudel, Weizi Li, Shuai Li
arxiv-2404-00796.description: Abstract Human-driven vehicles (HVs) exhibit complex and diverse behaviors. Accurately modeling such behavior is crucial for validating Robot Vehicles (RVs) in simulation and realizing the potential of mixed traffic control. However, existing approaches like parameterized models and data-driven techniques struggle to capture the full complexity and diversity.

arxiv-2405-17955.creator: O. Deniz Akyildiz, Mark Girolami, Andrew M. Stuart, Arnaud Vadeboncoeur
arxiv-2405-17955.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by O. Deniz Akyildiz, Mark Girolami, Andrew M. Stuart, Arnaud Vadeboncoeur. Bayesian inversion is central to the quantification of uncertainty within problems arising from numerous applications in science and engineering. arxiv-2407-08409.title: On the stability of the ill-posedness of a quasi-linear wave equation in two dimensions with initial data in H 7 / 4 ​ ( ln ⁡ H − β ) H^{7/4}(\ln H^{-\beta})
arxiv-2407-08409.creator: Gaspard Ohlmann
arxiv-2407-08409.description: Abstract Abstract This article is the continuation of [ Ohl23 ] where we exhibited the ill-posedness of a quasi-linear wave equation in dimension 2 for initial data in H^{7/4}(\ln H^{7/4}) . Here, we look at modifications of the equation and show that the blow-up phenomenon still occurs.

arxiv-2408-05122.title: A proposed deep sea Neutrino Observatory in the Nanhai
arxiv-2408-05122.creator: Huiming Zhang, Yudong Cui, Yunlei Huang, Sujie Lin, Yihan Liu, Zijian Qiu, Chengyu Shao, Yihan Shi, Caijin Xie, Lili Yang
arxiv-2408-05122.description: Abstract Over the past ten years, several breakthroughs have been made in multi-messenger astronomy. Thanks to the IceCube Neutrino Observatory, the detection of astrophysical neutrinos was proved to be practical. However, due to the limited statistics and field of view, only a few sources have been associated with IceCube neutrinos, making new and larger neutrino telescopes necessary.

arxiv-2410-03505.title: Classification-denoising networks
arxiv-2410-03505.creator: Louis Thiry, Florentin Guth
arxiv-2410-03505.description: Abstract Image classification and denoising suffer from complementary issues of lack of robustness or partially ignoring conditioning information. We argue that they can be alleviated by unifying both tasks through a model of the joint probability of (noisy) images and class labels. Classification is performed with a forward pass followed by conditioning.

arxiv-2508-15337.title: Hierarchical Black Hole Mergers in AGN Disks: Tracing Massive Black Hole Growth Across Cosmic Time Volume: 398 Journal: MODEST-25
arxiv-2508-15337.creator: Maria Paola Vaccaro
arxiv-2508-15337.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Maria Paola Vaccaro. The dense and gaseous environments of active galactic nuclei (AGNs) can catalyze repeated mergers of stellar-mass black holes (BHs), potentially explaining the high-mass tail of binary black hole (BBH) mergers observed by LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA (LVK). We present a semi-analytical population synthesis framework that captures key physical processes in AGN disks, including gas capture, migration, binary pair-up, gas hardening, and dynamical binary-single interactions.

arxiv-2509-05801.title: time2time: Causal Intervention in Hidden States to Simulate Rare Events in Time Series Foundation Models
arxiv-2509-05801.creator: Debdeep Sanyal, Aaryan Nagpal, Dhruv Kumar, Murari Mandal, Saurabh Deshpande
arxiv-2509-05801.description: Abstract While transformer-based foundation models excel at forecasting routine patterns, two questions remain: do they internalize semantic concepts such as market regimes, or merely fit curves? And can their internal representations be leveraged to simulate rare, high-stakes events such as market crashes?

arxiv-2511-20344.title: The Curious Case of Analogies: Investigating Analogical Reasoning in Large Language Models
arxiv-2511-20344.creator: Taewhoo Lee, Minju Song, Chanwoong Yoon, Jungwoo Park, Jaewoo Kang
arxiv-2511-20344.description: Abstract Analogical reasoning is at the core of human cognition, serving as an important foundation for a variety of intellectual activities. While prior work has shown that LLMs can represent task patterns and surface-level concepts, it remains unclear whether these models can encode high-level relational concepts and apply them to novel situations through structured comparisons.

pmc-10909103.title: Cost-Effectiveness Analysis of Ultrasound Surveillance for Cholangiocarcinoma in an Endemic Area of Thailand
pmc-10909103.creator: Pavinee Laopachee, Surachate Siripongsakun, Pannapa Sangmala, Phetcharaphon Chanree, Pantajaree Hiranrat, Songpon Srisittimongkon
pmc-10909103.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Objective:This research aimed to analyze the cost-effectiveness of ultrasound surveillance for Cholangiocarcinoma (CCA) in a high-risk population residing in the northern region of Thailand and compare these results with the non-surveillance patients who presented with CCA. Methods:This was a retrospective descriptive study of two groups monitored and treated for CCA in the same institute, but differing as to whether ultrasound was included in the surveillance.

pmc-12362948.title: RBM15 enhances paclitaxel resistance in triple-negative breast cancer by targeting m6A methylation of TNFSF9 and inducing polarization of tumor-associated macrophages to M2 phenotype
pmc-12362948.creator: Jinkun Fu, Chao Wei, Yijian Chen, Xiaoming He, Kun Zhang
pmc-12362948.description: BackgroundTriple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) is one of the breast cancer subtypes with a poor prognosis, and the current main treatment modalities include surgical resection and adjuvant chemotherapy. However, the development of drug resistance in tumor cells to chemotherapeutic agents poses great challenges to anticancer treatment.MethodsBioinformatics analysis was used to screen the up-regulated genes in paclitaxel (PTX)-resistant TNBC cells.

It draws on entomology-related research from the establishment of FARF in 2008 to the present.

pmc-12966447.title: Mapping and revealing the tree biodiversity of the Brazilian Cerrado through biome-wide sampling efforts
pmc-12966447.creator: Andre L Giles, Lucas Del Bianco Faria, Hallefy Junio de Souza, Silvia Barbosa Rodrigues, Lúcia Chamlian Munari, Ricardo da Silva Ribeiro, Gustavo Stancioli Campos de Pinho, Michella Del Rei Texeira, Érico Dianese, Bruno Grillo, Rafael Carvalho, Raquel Álvares Leão, Ana Laura Trindade, Claudio Robert
pmc-12966447.description: Biodiversity is essential for maintaining ecosystem functionality, ensuring food security, regulating climate, and sustaining human well-being. Yet, in neglected biomes, biodiversity is often lost before many species can even be identified or studied. In Brazil, the Cerrado stands out as the most flora diverse savanna on the planet, but it remains critically underexplored.

pmc-13074910.title: Ecological Niche Modeling of the Narrow-Range Endangered Endemic Lepidium olgae in Uzbekistan
pmc-13074910.creator: Khusniddin Abulfayzov, Bekhruz Khabibullaev, Khabibullo Shomurodov, Natalya Beshko, Suluv Sullieva, Yaoming Li, Lianlian Fan
pmc-13074910.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Narrow-range endemic plant species are highly sensitive to environmental variability due to their restricted distributions and narrow ecological niches, yet quantitative assessments of such species in Central Asian mountain ecosystem remain limited. This study applied an ensemble species distribution modeling (SDM) approach to assess the ecological constraints and conservation efforts of Lepidium olgae, a strict endemic species of the Nuratau Mountains in Uzbekistan.
